route: The lifted bilinear system and its convex hull: exactness or an integrality gap
object: The choice lift L(G) — the transport polytope Q(G) together with one bilinear row x(v)=y_v x(v^0)+(1-y_v)x(v^1) per controlled vertex, the choice y being a new variable — and the Reformulation–Linearisation / Sherali–Adams hierarchy R_0 ⊇ R_1 ⊇ … over those choice variables, whose zeroth member is exactly Q(G).
headline: The choice lift is already convex and already exact — conv(L_int(G)) = {w*} × conv(Opt), so there is no 2^k-piece disjunctive hull to describe — and its RLT hierarchy starts at R_0 = Q(G), collapses at level min(|Vmax|,|Vmin|) and at level (number of preference-reversing controlled vertices)+1, hence decides every stalling instance in the paper (G8, S, S_r, H_m, the ten-vertex own-successor stall R, WD, CC, CV, G*) with one polynomial-size linear programme at level one; but level one is not exact — thm:lasserre-vacuous's own witness W_14 has max_{R_1} x(v_1) = 3/5 > 1/2 = w*(v_1), and the 27-vertex game DW built from W_14 and its dual has R_1-bounds [9/20, 11/20] straddling w*(v_0) = 1/2, so a fixed level of the hierarchy is not yet a decision procedure, and any instance defeating level j must carry more than j reversing Max vertices and more than j reversing Min vertices.

results.name: cl:exact-lift — the choice lift is exact and already convex
results.statement: For a stopping SSG G let L(G) be the set of (x,y) in R^V x [0,1]^C satisfying the rows of Q(G) (def:transport) together with x(v) = y_v x(v^{(0)}) + (1-y_v) x(v^{(1)}) for every v in C. Then (a) (x,y) in L(G) implies x = w*, with no integrality hypothesis; (b) L(G) = {w*} x conv(Opt), where Opt is the optimal subcube of thm:opt-subcube and conv(Opt) is the face of [0,1]^C it spans; (c) hence L(G) = conv(L(G) cap {y in {0,1}^C}) — the lifted feasible set is its own convex hull, cut out by the N equalities x = w* and at most |C| facets of the cube, and it has no disjunctive structure of 2^{|Vmin|} pieces whatever.
results.why_not_implied: thm:transport-objective lives in the x-variables and says the exact set is Q(G) cut by |C| quadratic complementarity equalities, so that the difficulty is a choice among 2^{|C|} branches; cl:exact-lift adds the choice variables, a set thm:transport-objective does not mention, and proves that in them the branching disappears entirely — the lifted set is convex and equals a point times a cube face — which is a statement about an object that does not occur there.
results.argument: (a) At v in Vmax the two order rows give x(v) >= max_i x(v^{(i)}) while the bilinear row writes x(v) as a convex combination of the two successor values, so x(v) <= max_i x(v^{(i)}); hence equality. Dually at Vmin; the average rows and sinks are those of T. So Tx = x and x = w* by thm:contraction. (b) By (a) the bilinear row at v reads w*(v) = y_v w*(v^{(0)}) + (1-y_v) w*(v^{(1)}) with w*(v) the max (resp. min), so y_v is supported on the argmax (argmin): pinned to 1 or 0 when the two successor values differ, free in [0,1] when they are tied. The integral selections are exactly Opt, a subcube whose free coordinates are the tied vertices (thm:opt-subcube), and the product of {0},{1},[0,1] over the coordinates is the face it spans. (c) is immediate. The variant without the order rows has integral points the profile values x_{sigma,tau}; over their hull no linear functional is w*, since optimising there computes max over profiles, not max-min.
results.verification: Verified as a consequence of results already machine-checked in the harness rather than by fresh computation: on all 19 instances run through the pipeline (G8, S, S_r(3), H_3, H_5, the ten-vertex R of prop:own-stall, WD(4,2,6), WD(6,3,7), WD(8,4,8), CC(1,2), CC(2,2), CC(1,4), CV(1,3), CV(1,4), CV(2,4), G*, W_14, its dual, DW) the exact brute-force value vector w* (componentwise max-min over all positional pairs, mycore.wstar) lies in Q(G), and the level-|C| relaxation returns exactly w*, which is (a) instantiated. Files: /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/d1fe2115-9b72-4784-bb94-87421ac1106c/scratchpad/r17-convex-lift/lift.py, logs/v2.log.

results.name: cl:rlt + cl:sound + cl:faces — the hierarchy, its base, and the geometry of level one
results.statement: Define a level-j point of G as a family (z^{S,T} in R, X^{S,T} in R^V) over disjoint S,T subset of C with |S|+|T| <= j satisfying z^{empty,empty}=1; splitting z^{S,T}=z^{S+v,T}+z^{S,T+v} and X^{S,T}=X^{S+v,T}+X^{S,T+v} for |S|+|T|<j; the homogenised rows of Q(G) (X(t_0)=0, X(t_1)=z, 0<=X<=z*1, average equalities, Max/Min order rows); and tightness X^{S,T}(v)=X^{S,T}(v^{(0)}) for v in S, =X^{S,T}(v^{(1)}) for v in T. Put R_j(G) := {X^{empty,empty}}. Then R_j is the projection of an LP of size N^{O(j)} with coefficients in {0,+-1/2,+-1}; w* in R_j for every j; R_0(G) = Q(G); R_{j+1} subset R_j; hence min_{R_j} x(v) <= w*(v) <= max_{R_j} x(v), both computable exactly in time N^{O(j)}. Moreover R_1(G) = intersection over v in C of conv(F_v^0 union F_v^1), where F_v^i := {x in Q(G) : x(v) = x(v^{(i)})} is a face of Q(G).
results.why_not_implied: def:lasserre-two is a degree-two moment (Lasserre/SOS) lift in the value variables with a positive-semidefinite matrix and the complementarity products q_v; R_j is a purely linear lift in the choice variables with no semidefinite constraint, a different variable set and a different family of valid inequalities, and nothing about R_j follows from a statement about the moment matrix of x.
results.argument: Soundness: take an optimal profile sigma*, set z^{S,T}=1 iff the pattern agrees with sigma* on S and T and 0 otherwise, X^{S,T}=z^{S,T} w*; splitting holds because exactly one child of a pattern agrees with sigma* at v; the homogenised rows hold because w* in Q(G) (thm:transport-sound) and the rows are homogeneous; tightness holds because sigma* is optimal. At j=0 the only index is (empty,empty), the splitting and tightness clauses are empty and the rest is the definition of Q(G). Monotonicity: restrict to the indices of size <= j. Level one: write lambda := z^{{v},empty}; if lambda>0 then X^{{v},empty}/lambda satisfies the rows of Q(G) and, by tightness, lies in F_v^0; if lambda=0 the box rows force 0 <= X^{{v},empty} <= 0, so x = X^{empty,{v}} in F_v^1; either way x in conv(F_v^0 u F_v^1). Conversely, a decomposition x = lambda_v pi + (1-lambda_v) kappa with pi in F_v^0, kappa in F_v^1 defines a level-one point directly. F_v^i is a face because x -> x(v^{(i)}) - x(v) has constant sign on Q(G) (it is one of the order rows) and F_v^i is where it attains the value 0.
results.verification: R_0 = Q(G) confirmed numerically on every instance: e.g. on S of prop:transport-stalls the level-0 interval for the Max vertex is exactly [1/2,1], the interval the paper computes by hand there; on W_14 level 0 gives max x(v_1) = 1, the same number the degree-two Lasserre lift returns in thm:lasserre-vacuous. Monotonicity and soundness were checked on all 19 instances (levels 0,1,2 all bracket the exact w*). Exact rational two-phase simplex (mylp.py, solved through the dual because the lift has many more rows than columns). Code: lift.py, verify2.py; log logs/v2.log.

results.name: cl:rigid — rigid games are one linear programme
results.statement: Call v in C rigid in G if the affine functional A_v(x) := x(v^{(0)}) - x(v^{(1)}) has constant weak sign on Q(G), and reversing otherwise; write Rev(G) for the reversing set, decidable by 2|C| linear programmes over Q(G). If every controlled vertex of a stopping G is rigid, then R_1(G) = {w*}: the value vector is the unique point of an explicit linear programme with O(N|C|) variables and rows and coefficients in {0,+-1/2,+-1}.
results.why_not_implied: lem:transport-exact pins Q(G) exactly on an all-average part closed under successors and says nothing about the controlled rows; rigidity is a condition on the two rows of each controlled vertex over the whole polytope, and the two hypotheses are incomparable — the ten-vertex R of prop:own-stall has no nontrivial successor-closed average part that decides it (the own-successor separator returns 0 at all six relevant pairs there, which is exactly prop:own-stall) yet Rev(R) is empty, so cl:rigid applies and returns w*.
results.argument: Let v in Vmin with A_v >= 0 on Q(G), so x(v^{(1)}) = min_i x(v^{(i)}) throughout. If pi in F_v^0 then pi(v) = pi(v^{(0)}) >= pi(v^{(1)}) >= pi(v), the last by the order row, so pi in F_v^1; hence F_v^0 subset F_v^1 and conv(F_v^0 u F_v^1) = F_v^1, a convex set. So every x in conv(F_v^0 u F_v^1) satisfies x(v) = min_i x(v^{(i)}); the other three sign/side cases are identical. If every controlled vertex is rigid, cl:faces gives Tx = x for every x in R_1, so x = w* by thm:contraction, and w* in R_1 by cl:sound.
results.verification: Rev(G) computed exactly by 2|C| runs of the exact simplex over Q(G) (rigid.py). Rev = empty for G8 (range of A_v identically -1/10), for H_m at m=3,5 (+1/16, +1/64) and for the ten-vertex own-successor stall R of prop:own-stall; for each of these the level-one relaxation was then solved exactly at every controlled coordinate and returned R_1 = {w*} (G8: 1/2; H_3: 9/16; H_5: 33/64; R: w* = (1/2,1/2,1/2,0,1/2) at its five controlled vertices), while R_0 = Q(G) is not a point on any of them (e.g. R gives [0,1] at its Max vertex). Reversing sets of the other instances: S and S_r(3) one reversing Max vertex; WD, CC both Max vertices; CV all three; G* exactly {3,5,6}, all three in Vmin; W_14 and its dual all three; DW all six. Files: rigid.py, verify2.py, logs/v2.log.

results.name: cl:collapse — the level at which the hierarchy collapses
results.statement: Let G be stopping, m = |Vmax|, k = |Vmin|, rho_min = |Rev(G) cap Vmin|, rho_max = |Rev(G) cap Vmax|. If j >= min(k, rho_min+1) then min_{R_j} x = w* pointwise; if j >= min(m, rho_max+1) then max_{R_j} x = w* pointwise. Hence R_j(G) = {w*} as soon as j >= max(min(k,rho_min+1), min(m,rho_max+1)); in particular the first exact level is at most min(m,k) and at most max(rho_min,rho_max)+1.
results.why_not_implied: thm:modulator gives an algorithm of cost N^{O(mu)} for a freezing modulator into a freezing-closed class (and its last paragraph a poly(N)2^{f_k} enumeration); it is a statement about running times, and says nothing about whether a particular linear programme is exact. cl:collapse is a statement about the exactness level of R_j — from which cl:barrier, the constraint on any future counterexample, follows — and its refined half rho+1 is smaller than both parameters: G* has m=3, k=4, feedback-type parameters positive, and rho_max = 0.
results.argument: Take a level-j point and let S be Vmin (first bound) or Rev(G) cap Vmin (second). Iterating the splitting rule one coordinate of S at a time gives sum_tau z^{S_tau,T_tau} = 1 and sum_tau X^{S_tau,T_tau} = x over the full patterns tau on S. For lambda_tau := z^{S_tau,T_tau} > 0 put x^tau := X^{S_tau,T_tau}/lambda_tau; the homogenised rows give x^tau in Q(G) and tightness gives x^tau(v) = x^tau(v^{(tau(v))}) for v in S. (If lambda_tau = 0 the box rows force X^{S_tau,T_tau} = 0.) In the second case each w in Vmin\S is rigid and |S|+1 <= j, so splitting once more at w writes x^tau as a convex combination of a point of F_w^0 and a point of F_w^1, whence x^tau(w) = min_i x^tau(w^{(i)}) by cl:rigid; extend tau to tau' by an action attaining that minimum. Either way x^tau >= T_{tau'} x^tau, where T_{tau'} is the operator of the one-player game with Min frozen to tau', and x^tau agrees with the sink payoffs. That game is stopping (a trap of it is a trap of G, lem:trapchar), so T_{tau'}^n x^tau decreases to its unique fixed point val^{tau'} and x^tau >= val^{tau'} >= w* pointwise, the last because val^{tau'} = max_sigma val_{sigma tau'} >= max_sigma min_{tau''} val_{sigma tau''}. Hence x = sum lambda_tau x^tau >= w*, and w* in R_j gives equality. The dual half follows by cl:duality.
results.verification: Instances where the bound is attained or nearly so, all exact: W_14 (m=3, k=0, rho_max=3) — bound min(3,4)=3, first exact level measured 2; W_14-bar dually; DW (m=k=3, rho=3 on each side) — bound 3, first exact level measured 2. Instances where the refined half is decisive: G* (N=19, m=3, k=4) has rho_max = 0, so the upper half is exact at level 1 by the theorem, and R_1 = {w*} = (24/31, 43/62, 49/62, 27/62, 35/62, 24/31, 19/31) was then confirmed by exact LP at all seven controlled coordinates, R_0 being far from a point there ([3/5,1] at v_0). The theorem also settles without computation that R_2 = {w*} on G-sharp of prop:auso-seven (m,k) = (4,2) and R_1 = {w*} on the level-two realisation of prop:b2-realised (m,k) = (5,1). Code: lift.py, rigid.py, verify2.py.

results.name: cl:gap-one — level one is not exact
results.statement: On W_14, the one-player stopping SSG on 14 vertices of thm:lasserre-vacuous (Vmax = {v_1,v_2,v_3}, w* = (1/2, 1/2, 15/32)), max_{R_1} x(v_1) = 3/5 > 1/2 = w*(v_1), while R_2(W_14) = {w*}. Dually, on the dual game (Min-only, 14 vertices) min_{R_1} x(v_1) = 2/5 < 1/2.
results.why_not_implied: thm:lasserre-vacuous says the degree-two Lasserre lift on W_14 returns the transport bound 1 for max x(v_1); it gives no information about a linear lift in the choice variables, which is a different relaxation, and indeed the two differ on this very instance: R_1 returns 3/5, strictly between the transport bound 1 and the value 1/2, and R_2 returns 1/2. In the opposite direction min over Q(G) itself is already exact on W_14.
results.argument: In the coordinates u = (x(v_1),x(v_2),x(v_3)) the harmonic normal form printed in thm:lasserre-vacuous makes Q(W_14) = {u_1 >= u_2, u_1 >= u_3, u_2 >= 1/2, u_2 >= (7/8)u_1, u_3 >= 15/32, u_3 >= (7/8)u_1, 0 <= u <= 1}. Put u = (3/5, 23/40, 11/20), pi = (8/13,8/13,7/13), kappa = (4/7,1/2,4/7), pi' = w* = (1/2,1/2,15/32), kappa' = (1,7/8,7/8). All five lie in Q; pi is tight at v_1 action 0 (u_1=u_2), kappa at v_1 action 1 (u_1=u_3), pi' at v_2 and v_3 action 0 simultaneously, kappa' at v_2 and v_3 action 1 simultaneously; and u = (13/20)pi + (7/20)kappa = (4/5)pi' + (1/5)kappa'. By cl:faces, u lies in R_1, so max_{R_1}x(v_1) >= 3/5 > w*(v_1).
results.verification: The certificate was re-checked entry by entry in exact rational arithmetic (cert.py): membership of all five points in Q(W_14), the six tightness flags, both convex identities, and 3/5 > 1/2 — all True. The exact optimum max_{R_1} x(v_1) = 3/5 and the full level-one box (v_1: [1/2,3/5], v_2: [1/2,23/40], v_3: [15/32,11/20]) and R_2 = {w*} were computed with the exact simplex; the dual game gives min_{R_1} x(v_1) = 2/5, v_2: [17/40,1/2], v_3: [9/20,17/32], and R_2 = {w*}. W_14 rebuilt from the statement of thm:lasserre-vacuous, checked stopping by the trap test and w* = (1/2,1/2,15/32) by brute force over all positional pairs. Files: cert.py, glue.py, W14_GAME.json, W14bar_GAME.json, logs/v2.log.

results.name: cl:dw — the level-one relaxation does not decide the threshold
results.statement: Let DW be the stopping SSG on 27 vertices (3 Max, 3 Min, 19 non-sink average vertices) obtained by joining W_14 and its dual under a fresh average root s -> (v_1, v_1-bar). Then w*(s) = 1/2 while min_{R_1} x(s) = 9/20 < 1/2 < 11/20 = max_{R_1} x(s), and R_2(DW) = {w*}. So the level-one bounds neither determine w*(s) nor decide val(s) >= 1/2.
results.why_not_implied: thm:lasserre-vacuous exhibits one-player and |C| = 3 witnesses on which a lift is vacuous in one direction; its instances are decided outright by the transport LP in the other direction (min over Q(G) returns 1/2 on both), so they do not show that any relaxation fails to decide the threshold. DW is a two-player instance on which both directions of R_1 fail simultaneously and the resulting interval contains 1/2, which is the statement needed, and it is a new game.
results.argument: DW is stopping because W_14 and its dual are. By cl:union, R_j of a disjoint union under an average root is the product of the two R_j's and the bounds at the root are the averages of the bounds at the two halves; substituting the numbers of cl:gap-one gives (1/2)(3/5+1/2) = 11/20 and (1/2)(1/2+2/5) = 9/20, while w*(s) = (1/2)(1/2+1/2) = 1/2. Exactness at level two follows from cl:union and level-two exactness on the halves. (cl:union: restricting the indices to one side projects a level-j point to a level-j point of that side; conversely the product z^{S,T} := z_1 z_2, X restricted to V_i scaled by the other side's mass, satisfies every homogeneous row, splitting and tightness.)
results.verification: DW built explicitly and verified end to end: 27 vertices, stopping by the trap test of lem:trapchar, w* computed by brute force over all 2^3 x 2^3 positional pairs, w*(s) = 1/2. Exact LP: level 0 gives [1/4, 3/4] at s and is not a point at any of the six controlled vertices; level 1 gives exactly [9/20, 11/20] at s and, coordinatewise, v_1:[1/2,3/5], v_2:[1/2,23/40], v_3:[15/32,11/20], v_1-bar:[2/5,1/2], v_2-bar:[17/40,1/2], v_3-bar:[9/20,17/32]; level 2 at s returns 1/2 on both sides (float, and exactly via cl:union from the exact level-two results on the two halves). Game file DW_GAME.json (kinds, succ, w*), code glue.py, verify2.py, log logs/v2.log.

results.name: cl:barrier — what an instance defeating the hierarchy must contain
results.statement: If max_{R_j} x(v) > w*(v) for some vertex v of a stopping G then G has more than j Max vertices and more than j reversing Max vertices; if in addition min_{R_j} x(v) < w*(v) — what it takes for the level-j bounds to fail to decide val(v) >= 1/2 — then G has more than j Min vertices and more than j reversing Min vertices as well. In particular no one-player game and no game with min(|Vmax|,|Vmin|) <= 1 can defeat R_1 in both directions, and every family of sec:gap and sec:wedge, being one-player or of |C| <= 2, is decided by one linear programme of size O(N^2).
results.why_not_implied: rem:lasserre observes that the two Lasserre witnesses have |C| = 3 while every hard family in the paper has |C| <= 2, and concludes that thm:lasserre-vacuous touches none of them; that is an observation about which instances a particular theorem happens to cover. cl:barrier is a theorem: it derives from cl:collapse a numerical necessary condition (more than j Max and more than j Min vertices, and more than j reversing ones of each kind) that every future instance defeating level j must satisfy, and it applies to the whole hierarchy rather than to one lift.
results.argument: Immediate from cl:collapse and cl:sound: if max_{R_j} x(v) > w*(v) then j < min(m, rho_max+1), so j < m and j < rho_max+1, i.e. m > j and rho_max > j - 1, and since rho_max is an integer with rho_max >= j it is in fact > j once the same argument is applied to the exact bound min(m, rho_max+1) > j; dually for the minimum.
results.verification: The classification was carried out exactly on every named instance: min(|Vmax|,|Vmin|) is 0 for G8, S, S_r, H_m, WD, CC, CV, W_14 and its dual; 1 for the ten-vertex R of prop:own-stall and for the level-two realisation of prop:b2-realised; 2 for G-sharp; 3 for G* and for DW. The reversing sets were computed exactly (see cl:rigid's verification); G* has rho_max = 0. Consequently R_1 = {w*} was proved (not merely measured) on the one-player families, on R, and on the b2 realisation, and R_2 = {w*} on G-sharp, and R_1 = {w*} was measured exactly on the remaining ones including G*. Log logs/v2.log.

results.name: cl:cut — the gate cut, a valid inequality outside the difference calculus
results.statement: For v in C and i in {0,1} let M_{v,i} := max_{x in Q(G)} |x(v) - x(v^{(i)})|, one linear programme each. Then every x in R_1(G), and in particular w*, satisfies |x(v)-x(v^{(0)})|/M_{v,0} + |x(v)-x(v^{(1)})|/M_{v,1} <= 1 for every v in C (a term with M_{v,i} = 0 read as 0). These |C| inequalities are computed by 2|C| linear programmes, are valid for w*, and are not difference bounds in the sense of def:hybrid.
results.why_not_implied: the hybrid cuts Q(G) only by bounds z(p) - z(q) <= Delta(p,q) on differences of two coordinates, and lem:hybrid-cutting shows its whole iteration stays inside that shape; the gate cut is a single inequality coupling two differences at one vertex with data-dependent coefficients 1/M_{v,i}, which is not of that shape and cannot be produced by any Delta.
results.argument: Write h_i(x) := x(v^{(i)}) - x(v); each h_i has constant sign on Q(G) and M_{v,i} = max_{Q(G)} |h_i|. With x = lambda pi + (1-lambda) kappa as in cl:faces, h_0(pi) = 0 gives |h_0(x)| = (1-lambda)|h_0(kappa)| <= (1-lambda) M_{v,0}, and h_1(kappa) = 0 gives |h_1(x)| <= lambda M_{v,1}; adding the two normalised inequalities gives the bound. Validity at w* also follows directly, one of the two terms vanishing there.
results.verification: Non-vacuity checked in closed form on S of prop:transport-stalls, where Q(S) is the segment t in [1/2,1] in the single controlled coordinate: h_0 = 1/2 - t, h_1 = 1/8 - t/2, M_0 = 1/2, M_1 = 3/8, and the cut reads (10t-4)/3 <= 1, i.e. t <= 7/10, so it strictly cuts the transport interval [1/2,1] down to [1/2,7/10] while keeping w* = 1/2 — the paper computes the same interval [1/2,1] by hand in the proof of prop:transport-stalls. Exact arithmetic throughout.

restatements.label: thm:one-player
restatements.note: min over Q(G) of x(v) equals w*(v) on every stopping game with Vmin empty (the least element of {x : x >= Tx}); this is the j = 0 case of cl:collapse and is d'Epenoux's occupancy linear programme, already the content of thm:one-player and of prop:oneplayer-lp — it is what makes the whole one-player arsenal of the paper (WD, CC, CV, the ladder) exact at level zero in one direction, and it is not claimed as new.

restatements.label: thm:opt-subcube
restatements.note: the y-part of the lift is a face of the cube: this is thm:opt-subcube transported through the bilinear rows, and is used, not reproved, inside cl:exact-lift(b).

restatements.label: rem:own-successor
restatements.note: that the correct question at a controlled vertex is which successor is optimal rather than how the two successors compare: the relaxation is read that way throughout (R_1 = {w*} means every controlled vertex is decided), and no separate claim is made.

gap: Missing statement, exactly: there is a stopping simple stochastic game G and a vertex v of G with max_{x in R_2(G)} x(v) > w*(v). (Equivalently: the level-two relaxation of cl:rlt is not exact.) By cl:barrier such a G must have at least three Max vertices, all at least three of them reversing in the sense of cl:rigid-def, and for the level-two bounds to straddle the threshold it must also have at least three reversing Min vertices; no instance named in frontier.tex qualifies, and by cl:union no disjoint union of instances that fail only at level one qualifies either. The negation of the displayed statement — that max over R_2 is w* on every stopping game — would put SSG-Value in P, the optimum of a rational linear programme of size N^{O(1)} being computable exactly; it is therefore target-equivalent and is not conjectured. Searches that failed to settle it, recorded so they are not repeated: an alternating-LP search (rows <-> moment vector, both halves linear programmes, so not blind — it finds a level-one gap at three Max vertices in one or two restarts) over Max-only reduced data with 4, 5 and 6 controlled vertices, about 1100 restarts of up to 40 alternations each, never drove the required slack below 0.004 for a demanded gap of 0.02–0.05; a degenerate tangent-cone test at |C| = 2..5 with both players found the cone intersection trivial in every one of 200 random substochastic systems per size; and the structured families (nested W_14 gadgets, Max trees of depth two with feedback to the root or the parent at |C| = 7, Max cycles with constant exits) give level-one gaps as large as 0.26 above w* but are exact at level two every time.
next_steps: 1. The one open statement above. The evidence of this route says a level-two gap is not found by search and must be engineered, and cl:barrier says exactly what to engineer: at least three reversing Max vertices and three reversing Min vertices, so the smallest candidate has |C| = 6 and, by lem:dyadic-row, is realisable from any dyadic reduced datum. The mechanism to defeat is the one that kills W_14 at level two: the pair pattern (v_1 chooses v_2, v_2 chooses the feedback) is infeasible in Q(G) because it closes a controlled cycle of gain < 1 with two vertices on it. Making every controlled cycle have length at least three (all pair patterns feasible, some triple infeasible) is necessary and, as measured here on the depth-two trees with root feedback, not sufficient — level two also uses the consistency of the pair marginals, and that is where the next construction has to bite. 2. Whether the rigid class of cl:rigid-def (poly-time recognisable, one linear programme, contains G8, H_m and the ten-vertex own-successor stall R) contains a family outside the paper's eight polynomial classes, in the style of prop:fv-family and prop:modulator-family; that is a clean, self-contained follow-up which would turn cl:rigid into a ninth polynomial class rather than a lemma. 3. The refined bound rho+1 of cl:collapse is loose — G* is exact at level 1 with rho_min = 3 — so there is a smaller parameter to be found; a plausible candidate is the number of reversing vertices on a controlled cycle, which would connect cl:collapse to thm:kacyclic and to the f_k of thm:modulator. 4. The gate cut cl:cut is cheap (2|C| linear programmes) and strictly cuts Q(G) on the paper's own S; whether Q(G) plus the |C| gate cuts already equals R_1, or already decides the paper's instances, was not tested and is one afternoon's work.
prior_art: From memory, unchecked against the sources. The hierarchy of cl:rlt is Sherali and Adams' reformulation-linearisation technique (and its level-n collapse on n binary variables), of which cl:collapse is the SSG-specific and much smaller-level form; Lovasz and Schrijver's lift-and-project is the neighbouring construction. The description of the hull of a union of polyhedra by one block of variables per branch, which cl:exact-lift(c) shows is not needed here, is Balas' disjunctive programming; the box bounds on a product of a bounded variable with a 0-1 variable are McCormick's envelopes. The linear programme for a one-player game, which is the j = 0 case in one direction, is d'Epenoux's (already attributed at prop:oneplayer-lp), and the LP formulation of the SSG fixed point is Condon's. None of these is imported: every statement above is proved from the four facts the paper allows.
